messages:
mira: quick sync — we need a compact competitor script + one-pager for sales by end of week. goal: 2-minute rebuttals, 1-slide technical diff, and a single benchmark line for pitch decks.
elaine: +1. can we standardize the benchmark language? ops wants 'median p90 latency' and 'cost per 1k tokens' not vague percentages.
jim: for infra vendors emphasize "unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private" — that hits ops and platform teams. also put fallback policies in the FAQ.
beth: sales ask: short lines for the common objections please. e.g., "why not just use CloudAI's managed endpoints?" Need 3 quick bullets.
samir: putting suggested sales bullets here — please iterate: 1) Predictable economics: reserved/dedicated tiers avoid surprise egress + opaque bundling. 2) Unified API across modes — one integration for hosted and private. 3) Quality guardrails & rollouts (canary + auto-fallback) — reduces incident risk.
mira: nice. elaine can you craft a <30-word opener for the webinar that highlights the benchmark narrative?
elaine: draft — "See how teams cut inference cost and tail latency without rewriting infra: a live look at routing, caching, and quantization in production." thoughts?
beth: short objection scripts (sales-ready):
- Customer: "We already use CloudAI endpoints."
  - Rep: "Cloud endpoints are simple, but for production at scale teams trade predictability. Redwood gives you a single API plus reserved capacity options and routing controls to keep latency and cost stable."
- Customer: "We host our own models."
  - Rep: "Great — Redwood Private plugs into your network and gives the same runtime/observability so your platform team doesn't rebuild serving stacks."
- Customer: "Open-source runtimes are cheaper."
  - Rep: "Upfront cost is one thing; ongoing ops, rollouts, and SLOs add hidden costs. We provide the runtime + operational tools to lower total cost of ownership."
mira: perfect, can we also add a 1-sentence technical diff for the one-pager vs CloudAI + vs LLM-API providers + vs infra-only vendors? keep each to 10-12 words.
jim: my pass:
- vs CloudAI: opinionated serving + reserved capacity for consistent latency and cost.
- vs LLM APIs: production tooling and rollouts, not just model access.
- vs infra vendors: turn-key runtime + managed fallback, not raw orchestration.
marketing-bot: reminder: attached assets folder updated: https://redwood.ai/marketing/q3/comp_refresh (internal). please proof by Thu EOD.
mira: next steps — elaine finalize the webinar opener + 1-slide tech diff. beth to validate objection bullets with two SDRs. jim to add a quick bench note with source links (p95 p99 numbers). samir to compile the one-pager draft. we'll reconvene Fri 10am. :thumbsup:
elaine: will do. tagging @beth for SDR check.
beth: got it, I'll run with SDRs and report back before Thu.
mira: thanks all — thread closed unless urgent updates.
